articles.title: ‘Monster data centers’ being built in Scotland for US tech companies met with protests
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Thousands of people took to the streets of Edinburgh on Saturday, November 14, to protest against the massive expansion of data centers in Scotland. “Developers want to build monster data centers across Scotland and sell them on to big US tech companies,” the Stop AI Data Centers Scotland coalition wrote in the protest announcement. “There are over 20 already proposed and more in the pipeline, which would demand twice as much electricity as Scotland’s peak usage. This has huge consequences for our energy bills, water, health, communities, climate and nature.” Dozens of organizations that joined the coalition and protest – including climate justice associations, anti-war groups, and trade unions – have demanded accountability from the Scottish government: a pause on expansion plans, proper

articles.title: Iran warns there will be no geographical limit to its retaliation
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: In the latest round of “tit-for-tat” attacks, Iran claimed it destroyed the US army’s early warning radar system in Bahrain on Friday, November 13, in retaliation to its attack against its telecommunication tower in Sirik earlier. In the statement , the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) also reiterated the warning to the “aggressor enemy to cease its aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz” and other countries aiding in its aggression. Meanwhile, the Iranian Navy claimed at least two more oil tankers caught fire after they violated its warnings and tried to enter the prohibited area of the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday.
